title: Assistant Accountant Salary: Hourly Rates, Award Coverage, and Casual Loading
description: Understand the assistant accountant salary in Australia: hourly rates, award coverage, casual loading, and super paid on top. Calculate annual pay from a 38-hour week.
salarySummary: For an assistant accountant not covered by an award, the minimum pay is the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, with casual loading and super paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for an assistant accountant in Australia?
faqs.a: If an assistant accountant is not covered by an award (for example, working directly for an accounting firm), the minimum hourly rate is the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. For casual employees, a 25% loading applies, making the minimum $33.05 per hour. If the employer is in an industry covered by an award such as the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award or the Clerks Award, the applicable award rate may be higher. Always check the relevant pay guide for the correct classification.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual salary from an hourly rate for an assistant accountant?
faqs.a: To estimate annual gross pay, multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time assistant accountant working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the assistant accountant salary rate?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of the salary or hourly rate. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, if an assistant accountant earns $52,245.44 per year, the employer must contribute an additional $6,269.45 in super. Casual loading is also paid on top of the base rate, not on top of the super.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Assistant Accountant Salary

If you’re looking at an **assistant accountant salary** in Australia, it helps to know how hourly rates translate into annual pay, what award coverage applies, and how casual loading and superannuation affect your take-home pay. This guide uses the latest figures from the Fair Work Commission and the Fair Work Ombudsman, along with the Australian Taxation Office’s tax rates, to give you a clear picture.

For a full-time assistant accountant working 38 hours per week, the basic calculation is: hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks. But the actual rate you receive depends on whether you’re covered by an award, your employment type (permanent or casual), and your employer’s industry.

## How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

The formula for annual gross pay is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the calculation becomes:

- **Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual pay is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44

If you’re paid a salary, you can reverse the calculation to find your equivalent hourly rate: divide your annual salary by 52, then by your weekly hours. For a fortnightly pay cycle, multiply the weekly amount by 2.

### Award Coverage and the National Minimum Wage

According to the Fair Work Ombudsman, accountants working for an accounting firm are not covered by an award. They are entitled to the National Minimum Wage and the National Employment Standards. Other accounts employees, such as bookkeepers or payroll officers, may be covered by awards like the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award or the Clerks Award if their duties match the classifications. The Miscellaneous Award does not cover professional employees, including accountants.

If you are award-free, your minimum pay is the National Minimum Wage: $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award-covered employees may receive higher rates depending on their classification and the award’s minimum wage increase (award minimum wages rose by 4.75% from 1 July 2026).

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). **Important:** When using the [timesheet](/), you enter the base hourly rate, and a checkbox adds the 25% casual loading. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your salary or hourly rate. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, on a $52,245.44 annual salary, the employer contributes an additional $6,269.45 in super. This is not deducted from your pay; it’s an extra cost for the employer.

### Fortnightly Pay and Tax

If you’re paid fortnightly, your gross pay is your weekly rate multiplied by 2. For the National Minimum Wage, that’s $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight. Tax is withheld based on the 2026–27 resident tax scale:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed).

## Using the Timesheet for Your Pay Calculations

The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top. The tool also estimates tax and super, but remember: it assumes a steady 38-hour week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is calculated at 12% of ordinary earnings and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.

For a more precise picture of your **assistant accountant salary**, check the relevant [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. If you’re covered by an award, the pay guide will list the minimum rates for your classification, including allowances and penalty rates. The [reference tables](/data) also provide historical rates and the National Minimum Wage order.

### Average Weekly Earnings Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics’ May 2026 Average Weekly Earnings report shows full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week. All employees total earnings (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These figures are higher than the National Minimum Wage and reflect the broader workforce. An assistant accountant’s salary will vary based on experience, location, and industry.

## Key Takeaways

- The minimum **assistant accountant salary** for award-free employees is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours).
- Casual loading adds 25% on top of the base rate.
- Superannuation is paid on top at 12% of ordinary earnings.
- Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to switch between hourly and annual figures.
- Always check your award coverage via the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) guide or the Fair Work Ombudsman.

This estimate is a starting point. For your actual pay and entitlements, refer to your employment contract, award, or enterprise agreement.
